purpose: Brand context for education and market perception. These profiles are not reliability ratings and do not create an automatic rupee premium without used-market evidence.

source_notes.name: J.D. Power 2026 India Two-Wheeler Initial Quality Study
source_notes.scope: New two-wheeler initial quality, 6,381 owners, over 80 models, 15 nameplates; this is not a long-term used-bike reliability measure.
source_notes.use: Context only; never treated as a used-bike reliability score.

source_notes.name: J.D. Power 2025 India Two-Wheeler Initial Quality Study
source_notes.scope: New two-wheeler initial quality, 6,503 owners, 80 models, 12 makes.
source_notes.use: Context only; illustrates that measured quality and owner perception can be tracked separately from used-market price.

royal-enfield.buyer_lens: Owners often buy an RE for the feel, sound and identity as much as the transport. In resale, condition, originality and maintenance history still matter more than sentiment alone.
royal-enfield.emotion: Some motorcycles are bought with a spreadsheet. Others are bought because they made you stop and look back.

hero.buyer_lens: High familiarity and everyday-use positioning can make a model easier for buyers to understand. Model-specific condition and maintenance still determine the individual bike.
hero.emotion: A dependable daily bike can become part of your routine without you noticing—until it is time to let it go.

honda.buyer_lens: Honda has broad market familiarity in India. MotoWorth treats that as market context, not proof that every Honda is equally reliable; model, year and service history remain decisive.
honda.emotion: For some riders, the appeal is simple: an engine they trust, a bike they know, and fewer surprises along the way.

bajaj.buyer_lens: Bajaj spans everyday and performance-oriented motorcycles. Buyer demand and resale behaviour can differ significantly by model, so MotoWorth keeps the brand lens separate from the model's market evidence.
bajaj.emotion: Some bikes are remembered for the commute. Others are remembered for the grin they gave you on an empty road.

tvs.buyer_lens: TVS has a broad Indian lineup across practical and enthusiast motorcycles. Model-level evidence matters more than a single brand-wide assumption.
tvs.emotion: When a bike feels right every time you start it, that routine can become part of what you are actually saying goodbye to.

yamaha.buyer_lens: Yamaha carries a strong performance identity in India. MotoWorth treats enthusiast demand as a market-perception signal; any actual price premium must come from comparable used-bike evidence.
yamaha.emotion: There are motorcycles you own. And there are motorcycles you wait all week to ride.

suzuki.buyer_lens: Suzuki is a Japanese manufacturer with a strong engineering-led identity. MotoWorth will not assume long-term reliability from nationality alone; service history and model-specific evidence matter.
suzuki.emotion: Some bikes earn their place quietly: smooth starts, familiar controls and an engine you look forward to hearing again.

kawasaki.buyer_lens: Kawasaki has a strong enthusiast and performance identity. That can affect buyer interest, but MotoWorth does not turn badge value into an automatic price premium without market evidence.
kawasaki.emotion: If the bike was a dream when you bought it, it is worth remembering that the feeling was part of the purchase—even if resale has to be measured differently.

ktm.buyer_lens: KTM's identity is strongly performance-oriented. Used-bike value is especially sensitive to model, riding history, modifications and maintenance quality.
ktm.emotion: Some bikes are chosen because they promise trouble-free miles. Others are chosen because they promise stories.

triumph.buyer_lens: Triumph combines heritage with modern performance. Emotional demand can matter in resale, while service history and model-specific evidence remain essential.
triumph.emotion: A motorcycle can be transport, hobby and identity at the same time. MotoWorth keeps the value honest without pretending the emotion is irrelevant.

ducati.buyer_lens: Ducati ownership can carry strong emotional and enthusiast appeal. For used buyers, condition, documented servicing and model-specific maintenance exposure are critical.
ducati.emotion: Some motorcycles are bought because they make your pulse change before the engine even starts.

aprilia.buyer_lens: Aprilia has a performance-led identity and a more specialist buyer pool in India. Liquidity and resale can therefore be model-specific and evidence-led.
aprilia.emotion: The bike you choose because it felt different is often the bike you remember longest.

bmw-motorrad.buyer_lens: BMW Motorrad combines premium positioning, technology and touring/performance appeal. Used valuation should pay close attention to service records, electronics and model-specific maintenance.
bmw-motorrad.emotion: Premium bikes are rarely bought for one reason. The machine, the badge and the journey all become part of the story.

harley-davidson.buyer_lens: Harley-Davidson has unusually strong brand identity and emotional demand. Resale remains model- and market-specific rather than guaranteed by the badge.
harley-davidson.emotion: For some owners, the motorcycle becomes part of the person they were when they rode it.

jawa.buyer_lens: Jawa's modern Indian offering leans on heritage and styling. MotoWorth will separate that emotional appeal from evidence about used-market clearing prices.
jawa.emotion: Sometimes the first thing you remember about a bike is how it made you feel before you even rode it.

yezdi.buyer_lens: Yezdi trades on heritage and distinctive character. Model-specific demand, service history and parts exposure should be checked before assigning resale value.
yezdi.emotion: Character is part of why people choose certain motorcycles—and why letting one go can feel different.

benelli.buyer_lens: Benelli attracts buyers through design and performance character. Used value should be anchored by actual comparable listings and ownership condition.
benelli.emotion: A striking motorcycle can stay memorable long after the numbers have changed.

moto-guzzi.buyer_lens: Moto Guzzi has a distinctive heritage and enthusiast appeal. A smaller buyer pool can make condition and local market evidence especially important.
moto-guzzi.emotion: Some engines have a personality of their own. That personality is difficult to fit into a depreciation table.

qjmotor.buyer_lens: QJ Motor is a newer name in the Indian market. Resale evidence should therefore be treated cautiously until longer market histories develop.
qjmotor.emotion: Every newer brand starts by asking riders to take a chance. Time and ownership data are what turn that chance into confidence.

keeway.buyer_lens: Keeway competes through distinctive styling and international positioning. Used-market liquidity should be verified locally rather than assumed.
keeway.emotion: Sometimes you buy the motorcycle because it simply looks like you.

cfmoto.buyer_lens: CFMoto brings a relatively newer performance proposition to India. MotoWorth will rely on model-specific market evidence rather than assuming a universal brand premium or discount.
cfmoto.emotion: A bike can be a statement before it becomes a statistic.

bsa.buyer_lens: BSA relies heavily on heritage and design identity. Resale value should be grounded in model-specific demand and condition.
bsa.emotion: Heritage is one of the few things you can feel before you put a bike into gear.

brixton.buyer_lens: Brixton is positioned around distinctive design and character. Used-market depth should be established with actual local comparables.
brixton.emotion: A bike that looks different can make the morning ride feel different too.

norton.buyer_lens: Norton carries a historic premium identity. For used buyers, parts, service support and local market liquidity deserve close attention.
norton.emotion: Some names carry stories that are older than the motorcycle sitting in your garage.

revolt.buyer_lens: Revolt sits in the electric-mobility market, where battery condition and technology cycle can materially affect used value.
revolt.emotion: The first bike that changed how you think about mobility can become a meaningful chapter in your ownership story.

ather.buyer_lens: Ather's product identity is strongly technology-led. For used value, battery health, software/support horizon and local service experience matter alongside age and kilometres.
ather.emotion: For some riders, the dashboard and charging routine become as familiar as an engine note.

ola-electric.buyer_lens: Ola Electric sits in a fast-changing EV market. Used valuation needs special attention to battery, software, support and model-year changes.
ola-electric.emotion: New technology can make a bike feel like a glimpse into the future—and that can be part of why it was chosen.

vida.buyer_lens: Vida's value is closely tied to the EV ownership experience. Battery condition and support ecosystem need to be checked directly.
vida.emotion: A different kind of ride can still become a very personal daily ritual.

simple-energy.buyer_lens: Simple Energy is a newer EV brand, so market-history and support data should be treated cautiously until a deeper used market develops.
simple-energy.emotion: Early adopters often remember the moment they chose something unfamiliar. That story is real, even when resale is still being discovered.

bgauss.buyer_lens: BGauss competes in urban electric mobility. Battery health, support and parts availability should be considered alongside age and kilometres.
bgauss.emotion: A scooter can still become the vehicle that carries years of small, important moments.

husqvarna.buyer_lens: Husqvarna sits within a performance-oriented family with distinctive design. Used value should be anchored in model-specific demand, condition and local comparable listings.
husqvarna.emotion: Some motorcycles are chosen because they look unlike anything else. That choice is part of the ownership story.

fallback.buyer_lens: A badge can influence what buyers expect, but MotoWorth will only turn that perception into a rupee adjustment when used-market evidence supports it.
fallback.emotion: A motorcycle is more than an asset to the person who owned it. MotoWorth keeps that in the conversation without pretending sentiment equals resale value.
